headline: MD and enhanced sampling reveal lipid and ion control of transporter gating
label: Molecular Dynamics Of Membrane Transporters
summary: Recent preprints and a published study apply all-atom and enhanced-sampling MD to resolve transporter energy landscapes in explicit membranes.
synthesis: Across these items, molecular dynamics quantifies how membrane transporters move between conformational states and how lipids and bound ions modulate those transitions. In NarU, adaptive sampling and Markov state models reveal outward-facing asymmetry and an apo-occluded state that enables symport. All-atom simulations of CFTR in a heterogeneous bilayer, comparing apo and VX-770-bound forms, map 557 electrostatic interactions linked to anion coordination and lipid contacts. Cryo-EM combined with enhanced-sampling MD shows that bicarbonate lowers and PIP2 raises the outward-to-inward transition barrier in AE1. The common thread is quantitative energy-landscape characterization of transporter gating, with lipids and ions treated as explicit modulators. What is new is atomic-level resolution of these couplings in heterogeneous membranes, although the NarU study addresses mechanistic diversity of MFS symport rather than lipid modulation.
